the trial split removes this cue, so performance falls to chance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["obs_1"],"limitations":"Cannot identify the specific feature or rule out coexisting genuine window signal; synthetic data only."},{"id":"H2","claim":"The high window score reflects a genuine window-level class signal that should generalize to unseen trials; the chance trial score is due to noise or split instability rather than trial-specific leakage.","mechanism":"Class-discriminative patterns are present in individual windows independent of trial identity, so trial isolation should retain some signal.","supporting_evidence_ids":["obs_1"],"limitations":"Baseline trial and subject scores are near chance, which is difficult to reconcile with a strong generalizable signal."}],"request_id":"req_1","tool_id":"trial_random_labels","parameters":{},"distinguishes":["H1","H2"],"prediction":{"scoring_status":"numeric","metric_key":"trial_random_gap_mean","primary_direction":"positive","threshold":0.05,"check_facts":[],"conditional_predictions":[{"hypothesis_id":"H1","direction":"positive","rationale":"Trial-level random labels remain learnable through same-trial windows, producing high window BA and chance trial BA, hence a positive gap."},{"hypothesis_id":"H2","direction":"near_zero","rationale":"With true trial labels randomized at the trial level, no genuine transferable window signal remains, so window and trial BA should both be near chance and the gap near zero."}],"update_rule_if_opposite":"If trial_random_gap_mean is near zero or negative, reject H1's trial-specific explanation and favor H2 or an unresolved noise/identity explanation."},"reasoning_summary":"Baseline shows near-perfect window BA but chance trial BA, suggesting same-trial leakage. Randomizing labels at trial level should still be learnable in a window split if trial-specific signatures drive performance, while a genuine window signal would not survive randomization."}
